THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 12, 1922

Light is shed by the interview
with Mr. K. S. Lee:
"When the seamen threatened to
strike," said, Mr. Lee, "the
owners thought they were not
serious and were only taking
advantage of the China New
Year Holidays.
One shipowner, at a meeting, is
reported to have said that the
seamen would be starving in a
week and they would be forced
to resume their work anyhow.
Then at the first meeting with
the Union leaders, the Secretary
for Chinese Affairs in the
Colony, Mr. Halifax, is report-
ed to have bluffed the men and
stated that, that—the first
meeting—would be the final
one and that the men would be
given no further chance—others
would be employed to take their
places, if they did not return
to work at once."
Can one wonder that workmen
strike for better conditions,
when on their own showing,
their masters rely on the wea-
pons of starvation and denial?
I am not surprised that the sea-
men are standing out for their
terms. Like countless other or-
ganised bodies of workmen,
they decline to be bluffed.
Much has been said by the em-
ployers' side about the Canton
Government, with the idea of
discrediting that Government
and belittling the efforts of the
seamen to improve their condi-
tion.

《字林西报》，1922年2月12日，星期六

李（K. S. Lee）先生的谈话阐明了事态：

“当海员威胁要罢工时，”李先生说，“船东们认为他们并非动真格，只不过是想利用中国新年假期占点便宜。

据称，在一次会议上，一位船东曾说，海员们在一周内就会挨饿，无论如何都将迫使他们复工。

接着，在与工会领导人的第一次会晤中，据称殖民地华民政务司哈利法克斯（Halifax）先生对工人们虚张声势，声称那——第一次会议——将是最后一次会议，如果工人们不立即复工，将不再给他们任何机会——并将雇用其他人来取代他们的职位。”

既然雇主们自己表明依赖饥饿和拒绝谈判作为手段，人们怎能不奇怪工人为争取更好条件而罢工呢？

我对海员们坚持其要求并不感到惊讶。像无数其他有组织的工人群体一样，他们拒绝被虚张声势所吓倒。

雇主方面说了许多关于广东政府的话，其目的是败坏该政府的声誉，并贬低海员为改善自身条件所作的努力。
